whatItIs.text: A dense head — the 'curd' — of undeveloped flower buds, usually white but also orange, purple, or the fractal-spiralled Romanesco.

historyNote.text: Cauliflower is an 'arrested inflorescence' of wild cabbage that arose around 2,500 years ago in the Mediterranean; the familiar orange type began as a single natural mutant found in a Canadian cauliflower field.

howToChoose.text: Choose heavy heads with tight, clean curds and fresh-looking leaves; brown spots or spreading florets mean age.

storage.text: Keep stem-down loosely wrapped in the fridge; once cut, use quickly. The rulebook has the window.
storage.note: storage windows live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Tired cauliflower roasts beautifully with olive oil until the edges blacken, or blitzes into soup; the stem, peeled, is the sweetest part.
